Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh had 4 centurions of their own with Mehidy almost touching 250. They have been mentally drained and will hope that their batsmen fight it out in this innings. Take it session by session, hour by hour. First aim - to go unscathed into Tea. 43 overs left in the day. Lose as few wickets as possible. Let's see how their reply unfolds.

An innings which was studded with three centurions, all in the top order. Both Raval and Latham threw their wickets away while skipper Williamson batted through. Barring Taylor, everyone played well and perhaps, one could question the feelings of Williamson towards de Grandhomme - could he have allowed Colin half an hour to get to his 100?

So, an hour after Lunch and the second innings of the match ends. The Black Caps have got a mammoth lead of 481 but the good signs for Bangladesh are that the pitch is still flat. The bowlers have got nothing and if any, it might just be the swing on offer early on.

Neil Wagner, the night watchman, entertained in his cameo of 47 from 35 balls, in a stand of 60 with his skipper while Watling just added to the misery of Bangladesh. Kane Williamson, in the meanwhile, has continued in his own merry way, reaching his century, going past 150 and now, looking good for a double ton.

That wicket before Lunch might brings smiles on the faces of Bangladesh but this match has galloped away from them at sheer pace. 154 runs have been conceded in this session, in 29.5 overs, for the wickets of Wagner and Watling. The lead is a massive 371 and it just seems like the case of water level rising above one's head.

PITCH REPORT - Craig Cumming it is, doing the pitch report again. Observes plenty of cracks today as well, indicating that they are widening up. But also sees that they are on the shorter side, so it should not be too much of an issue for the batsmen. May be, the odd ball might misbehave.
WEATHER REPORT - Another cloudless day. Bright sunshine. What a day to play cricket. A Saturday too. Pull up your feet on the sofa and enjoy the game.

Very rarely do you see triple figures three times in a scorecard, let alone in the first three batsmen. After tons by Latham and Raval, captain Kane is now on track for his 20th Test ton. Neil Wagner is in as a night watchman but the pitch has nothing in it, so expect him to hang around for a while.

A day of records. That is what we witnessed on a drubbing Friday. Why drubbing? Because that is how Bangladesh would have felt. When a 254-run opening stand takes place, you seldom feel like even fighting back. The visitors got flat and the hosts took full toll. With the lead reading 217, the Kiwis might just be comfortable with another 100 runs on the board but given that there is so much of time left in the game, do not be surprised if they continue to bat through the day. Can Bangladesh try and bowl them out? Hello and a warm welcome to the third day of the opening Test between New Zealand and Bangladesh in Hamilton.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Now then, what can we expect on Day 3? New Zealand on the charge after Williamson gets to his ton? Also, how long will New Zealand bat or how many more runs will they look to add? Also, if Bangladesh do bat on Saturday, will they be able to put up a fight? A lot of these questions should be answered. Do join us on the 2nd of March at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous night). Till then, take care and goodbye!

Earlier in the day, the Kiwi openers added 254, both getting to their tons. Williamson then joined Latham and the two added yet another vital stand before Tom and Taylor fell in quick succession. Bangladesh did get a sniff at that moment but Williamson's and Nicholls' 100-run stand has seen them end the day in the driver's seat.

Bangladesh though will argue they had a decent last session and if you compare it with the two sessions before this one, you will have to agree. They started the final session by taking Taylor and Latham quickly. Williamson and Henry though then stitched another handy stand, taking the lead in excess of 200. Both of them got to their respective fifties before a lapse in concentration led to the downfall of the left-hander. Wagner however, ensured that he along with his skipper, played out the remaining overs and ended Day 2 without losing any more wickets.

An outstanding day of cricket for the Kiwis comes to an end. One can probably say they have batted the visitors out of the game. They have stretched their lead to 217 and are yet not done. They still have six wickets in the bag and whole lot of time left.

Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls misreads the straighter one and leaves it alone. The ball comes in with the angle and goes onto hit the off pole. Bangladesh are up in celebration and Nicholls walks back with his head down. No hiding place for Nicholls and he will be reminded of that by his teammates and friends for a long time now.
On the stumps, Henry taps it back to the bowler.
On the pads, Nicholls flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Full on middle, Henry hits it straight. Mehidy dives to his left to stop the ball. He gets a hand to it and the ball hits Willamson's bat at the non striker's end and goes to the fielder at mid off.
Once again short outside off, Nicholls punches it to the fielder at cover.
Shorter on off, Williamson punches it towards long on and takes a single to bring up the 100-partnership between the two.
On the fuller side, it is driven to the man at covers.
Outside off, not played at.
Soumya Sarkar pulls out at the very end. Not very sure why but I feel he just might have felt he had overstepped there.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.

FOUR! If you slash, you should slash hard. Nicholls brings up his fifty with a streaky boundary. Short and wide outside off. HN throws his bat at it but it takes the outside edge and flies over the slip cordon for a boundary. His good form with the bat continues.
Shortish and outside off, it is slapped through covers for a single.
That came back in late! A good leave in the end. Length delivery outside off, it pitches and jags back in. Williamson makes a leave and it goes really close past his pad.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Very full again on middle, Nicholls flicks it through mid-wicket and a couple is taken.
Flighted ball and outside off, Williamson reaches out for it and drives it through covers for a single.
Very full and on the pads, it is flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Flighted ball on off, the batter strokes it to mid off.
On the stumps, it is kept out.
Driven crisply but can't beat the man at mid off.
Angles it into the off stump, KW gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
Outside off, Williamson shuffles across and lets it be.
Around the off stump, it is stroked through covers for a single.
Attacks the off pole again. HN pushes it to mid off.
Continues hitting the length on the off pole, Nicholls defends it out.
This time Mehidy bowls it on the pads, Kane flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Full on the stumps, Williamson defends it.

FOUR! Full marks to Liton Das for his effort though. Once again shorter in length, this time Williamson guides it towards third man. Sarkar puts in a dive to catch it but misses. However Liton does not give up and runs after it. He tries to stop the ball with his right foot and for a moment it looked like he did. But replays show he did not and it is another boundary for Williamson.

FOUR! Lucky escape for Williamson and another sloppy effort from Soumya Sarkar at slip. Shorter in length on off, the ball spins slightly away after pitching. Williamson looks to defend it but gets a thick outside edge. It flies past first slip. Soumya Sarkar there is slow to react and the ball goes away to the fence for a boundary.

Run out chance. Saved. Full on middle, Nicholls hits it towards mid on and goes for a quick single. The fielder takes too long to take his aim and then has a shy at the stumps at the bowler's end. He misses it but the replays show Nicholls was quick and would have been in.
Shorter on middle and off, Nicholls gets on his back foot and hits it back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Once again it is on a length, Williamson prods forward this time and keeps it out.
Good length again, Williamson stays back and defends it onto the ground.
Back of a length on off, Williamson stands tall and pushes it through covers.
On a good length and around off, it is kept out.
Outside off, an easy leave.
Loopy delivery on middle and leg, Kane keeps the strike by hitting it towards mid on.
Tossed up on the stumps, Williamson solidly defends it.

Poor from the fielding side. Flighted delivery on off, Nicholls defends it with soft hands and the ball goes towards cover. The batsmen look for a quick single and go for it. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses his shy at the stumps. There is no one backing up there which allows the batsman to get an extra couple. 3 runs taken overall.
Flighted on off, Henry blocks it.
Fuller this time on off and middle, Nicholls defends this one with a straight bat.
Shorter delivery on off, Nicholls gets on his back foot and hits it to the fielder at mid on.
Gets right behind the line this time and blocks it out.

Good comeback by the bowler. He has beaten Williamson on the inside. This starts from outside off and it comes back in a long way. Williamson looks to defend but does not account for the movement, it goes between his bat and pad.

FOUR! Class, sublime, you can call that anything you want. That was a top, top shot. There is an extra cover, cover and a mid off in place. Williamson still finds the gap as he caresses it through cover and extra cover for a boundary.
Outside off, this is guided through point and a single is taken.
On the fuller side outside off, Nicholls strokes it to cover.
Shortish and outside off, it is hit through point for an easy run.
Halt in play as Williamson is seen having a drink. Bizarre, as we had a Drinks break 15 minutes before.
Slightly shorter this on off and middle, Nicholls sees off the over with a classical front foot defense.
Lands it on middle and off, HN blocks it.
Tossed up on off, Henry carefully defends it.
On the off stump this one, Nicholls defends it with a straight bat.
Tossed up on middle, Williamson nudges it towards square leg for a single.
Shorter, away turner outside off, Nicholls gets on his back foot and slaps it towards covers for a single.
Goes wide of the crease and angles this one into the batsman, blocked out.
The yorker on middle, Williamson gets his bat down in time and keeps it out. Good bowling this.
On the stumps, Williamson strokes it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Short, wide and put away! Williamson waits for it to come to him and then guides it through backward point for a boundary.
On the fuller side outside off, Williamson strokes it to the man at mid off.
On the off stump, the batter blocks it onto the ground.
On the off stump, kept out. A good over by the offie comes to an end.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floats it up on off, Nicholls prods forward and keeps it out.
Flatter and on middle, Nicholls clips it to the man at mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on middle, Nicholls works it to mid-wicket.

Uppish but finds the gap! Lucky escape there for Nicholls. He looks to hit it against the turn but the ball grips a touch, takes the outside edge and lands safely in the cover-point region. A couple taken.
Finds the gap this time but only a single! Short and outside off, Nicholls cuts it through point and a run is taken.
Goes fuller in length and on off, Nicholls crisply drives it to mid off.
Another wide delivery outside off, Nicholls ends up chopping it in the cover region. He wants a run but is rightly sent back by his partner.
Way outside off, on a fuller length. Nicholls slaps it hard but finds the man at covers.
On the off stump again, kept out.
On a good length and around off, Nicholls opens the face of the bat and guides it to point. He sees whether the ball beats the fielder there, it does not and no run has been taken.
A loopy bouncer there, goes comfortably over Nicholls' head. Wide given.
Full on the stumps, Williamson watchfully blocks it. Mehidy has not troubled the batsman all day long and he needs to change his strategy here.
Flighted on off, Nicholls milks it towards mid off and rotates the strike.
On the pads again, Williamson nudges it wide of the fielder at mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg, Kane tucks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Flights this one and bowls it full on off, Henry pushes it towards mid off and takes a single.
Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls defends it.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson punches it nicely but straight to the fielder at cover.
Full and straight outside off, Williamson leaves it alone.
Full length delivery outside off, Nicholls hits a textbook drive to the fielder at deep point for a single.
Length delivery on the stumps, Nicholls defends it off his back foot.
Length delivery on off, Nicholls hits it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Full length delivery outside off, Henry leaves it alone.
Soumya Sarkar back on.
Lands it on off, Williamson defends it to see off the over.
On the stumps, KW blocks it off his front foot.
On middle and leg and Williamson picks out the same fielder again with his flick.
On the pads, Kane flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Too full this one to expect any spin off the surface. It is on middle and leg, Henry hits it towards mid on and takes a single.
Straighter one outside off, Nicholls pick it up early and leaves it alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Around off, watchfully pushed to the off side.

FOUR! BRUTAL! Normally, we don't use this adjective for Mr. Kane. He is so polite with his words and so gentle with his stroke-making. But not on this occasion. A gentle half-tracker, in the high 120s at max, sitting up and asking to be smashed. The generous Willy obliges and immediately rocks onto the back foot, pulling it with aplomb over mid-wicket. The lead is now 170.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Around off, solidly defended.
On a good length outside off, Williamson hops and flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
Flighted on the stumps, Nicholls defends it to finish this 8-run over.
Lands it full on the stumps, Henry defends it.
Slightly shorter and straighter outside off, Henry chooses to leave it alone.
FOUR! Nicholls going after Mehidy here. Flighted delivery on off, Nicholls takes the aerial route and lofts it over mid-wicket. The ball bounces before the ropes and goes away for a boundary.

FOUR! A very courageous shot from Nicholls. Tossed up delivery on off, Henry premeditates his shot and sweeps it towards the fine leg region for a boundary. 400 up for New Zealand and also the partnership between these two has crossed 50.

Interesting discussion between Mark Richardson and Scott Styris on air. The former Kiwi opener is irritated with the fact that now-a-days, many teams are struggling to bowl 90 overs in the stipulated time, taking that extra half hour almost inevitably.  He believes that it is the duty of the umpires to ensure that things speeden up. In response, Styris says that he has been told that in modern age cricket, the umpires actually check every 8 overs as to how the over rate is. Hmmm... well, still, there has not been much improvement. Maybe, a bit stricter punishment?
Flighted delivery, full on off, Henry defends it.

Drinks Break. A good session so far for Bangladesh on the context of the game. They have picked up two wickets but by no means New Zealand are in trouble here as Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls are looking good out in the middle.
On a length on off, Nicholls drives it towards covers for a single. 8 runs came from the over. Bangladesh are getting frustrated here and they have no answer to New Zealand's batting.
Length delivery on off, Henry plays it through covers. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to this one.
FOUR! Lovely shot from Henry Nicholls. Full and outside off, Nicholls drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
On a good length on off, Nicholls plays it to covers.
Length delivery on middle, Williamson flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Shorter in length, Kane defends it with soft hands and takes a single as the ball goes towards backward point.
Loopy delivery on off and middle, KW blocks it carefully.
Tossed up delivery on off, Nicholls looks to defend it but the ball spins back into him after pitching. He gets an inside edge and the ball goes to the on side and they take a single.

Excellent fielding. Shorter delivery just outside off, Williamson rocks onto his back foot and punches it through covers. The fielder chases the ball and does a good job. He pulls it back to his partner and saves a run for his side.
Flighted on off and middle, Kane defends it with straight bat.
Shorter off spinner on the middle and leg, Willaimson flicks it towards the fine leg region and gets a couple.
Mehidy Hasan back into the action.
On a good length on off, Nicholls looks to drive but it goes off the inner half of the bat. It goes towards square leg for a run.
Outside off, the skipper shoulders his arms to this one.
On a good length on middle, Henry defends it off the back foot.
On middle and leg, Williamson nudges it towards square leg for a run.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Nicholls flicks it towards the leg side for a run.
FOUR! Classic straight drive from Henry Nicholls. Full on middle, Nicholls drives it straight past the bowler for a boundary.
Khaled Ahmed brought back into the attack. Replaces Soumya Sarkar.
Length delivery on off, Henry plays it towards point for a run.

Ebadot is lucky to get away with that. That was a massive no ball. Not for overstepping but because the bowler cut the side crease with his back foot. As per the cricketing rules, one is not supposed to even touch the line, let alone cut it. Umpire Paul Reiffel has missed it. Coming to the ball, it was a length delivery on off, Williamson moved across and flicked it towards square leg for a run.
On middle and leg, Nicholls works it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Length delivery on middle, the skipper flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Again on a good length on middle, Williamson pushes it to mid on.
On a good length on off, Williamson defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on off, Kane pushes it towards covers and takes a single.
Good length delivery on off, Williamson this time blocks it off the middle of his bat.

Brilliant bowling. The outswinger is followed by an inswinger. Again on a length, Williamson looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball was almost going towards the stumps after hitting the pads but Kane stops it with his bat.
Slight away swing on this one. Length ball outside off, Williamson leaves it alone.
Back of a length delivery on off, Nicholls punches it on the off side and gets to the other end.

Full commitment. Good length delivery on off, Williamson brilliantly flicks it through mid-wicket. For a moment it looks like the ball will reach the fence but Tamim Iqbal does not give up the chase and pulls the ball before it reaches the fence. The batsmen come back for the third.
On a good length on middle, Nicholls keeps it out.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Nicholls chases this ball and it goes of the bottom edge towards third man for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle, Nicholls plays it to mid on.
Outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Short and outside off, the skipper cuts it through point for a run.
On a good length and outside off, Williamson plays it towards the bowler.
On a good length on middle, Nicholls defends it off the back foot.
Bowls it wide outside off, Henry lets it go.
On a good length and outside off, Nicholls leaves it alone.
Outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to this one.
Full outside off, Nicholls drives it towards covers.

50 for Kane Williamson. 30th Test fifty for him. It has been a decent knock from him. Short and outside off, Williamson slaps it through covers for a run. He has looked positive and his timing has been great.

FOUR! Great way to get off the mar. Length delivery on the pads, Nicholls times his flick excellently and the ball beats the chasing fielder and goes to the mid-wicket fence. That's the shot of a confident man on the first ball.
Length delivery on off and middle, Williamson tucks it towards square leg for a single and moves to 49.
Fuller this time on off, KW defends it off his front foot and shouts a loud no to his partner for a single.
Good length delivery, this time on middle and leg, Williamson solidly blocks it off his front foot.
Back of a length delivery around off, Kane punches it through cover point and gets a brace.
Good length delivery outside off, this goes away from the batsman. Williamson offers no shot to it and lets it go.
Henry Nicholls is the new man in. Ebadot Hossain is also back into the attack.

OUT! That was as plumb as it gets. Soumya Sarkar gets two in quick succession. On a good length on middle, Taylor looks to flick but misses it and gets hit on the pads. Sarkar appeals and the umpire raises his finger. Taylor doesn't think about the review as he knew he was out. He was a goner there. Hawk Eye shows that impact is in line and is hitting the leg stump. Soumya Sarkar did not have good time with the bat but he is doing well with the ball. The ploy to take the new ball has worked for Bangladesh.
Outside off, Taylor shoulders his arms to this one.
On middle, the skipper flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Length delivery on middle, Williamson flicks it to mid-wicket.
Short and outside off again, Taylor cuts it through point for a single.
Short and outside off, Taylor cuts it towards third man.
Length delivery outside off, Taylor plays it towards point and keeps the strike for the next over with a single.
On the pads, Williamson nudges it to the leg side for a single.
Good bowling. This one comes back in. Pitched outside off, Williamson is aware where his off stump is and leaves it. There's ohs and ahs from the Bangladeshi players.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson guides it to the fielder at gully.
Good length delivery on the fourth stump line, the ball goes away after pitching. Williamson leaves it alone.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Williamson flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Outside off, Taylor lets it go.
On a good length outside off, Ross looks to defend but gets beaten due to the away swing on this one.

APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! Full on middle and leg, Taylor looks to flick but misses it and gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Hawk Eye shows that the impact was outside leg and the ball was missing the leg stump.
Good shape on this one. Good length delivery outside off, Taylor looks to play inside the line but gets beaten due to the away movement on this one.
Length delivery on middle, the skipper flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Short and wide outside off, Williamson slaps it through covers. The batsmen pick up a couple.
On a good length outside off, Taylor lets it go. Maiden over from Abu Jayed.
On a good length on middle, Taylor defends it off the back foot.
No swing on this one. Outside off, Ross offers no shot to this one.
Outside off again, Taylor leaves it alone.
Poor delivery from Abu Jayed. Bowls down the leg side, Taylor looks to flick but misses it.
Good length delivery outside off, Taylor shoulders his arms to this one.

Good delivery to finish the over. Full length delivery on middle and off. The ball moves away after pitching, Williamson looks to defend it but gets a leading edge and the ball goes towards the fielder at point.
Another good shot. Length delivery outside off, Kane cuts it excellently but straight to the fielder at point.
FOUR!!! Excellent shot. Full length delivery on off, Williamson gets on his front foot and drives it through extra cover for a boundary.
Good bowling. Length delivery on off, the ball comes in after pitching. Williamson looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Little inswing on this one. Pitches it on the fifth stump line, Williamson knows where his off stump is and he leaves it confidently.
Length delivery on the off stump line, Kane defends it.
Swing straight away with the second new ball. Full toss on the fourth stump line, Taylor hits it through the gully region and gets a couple to finish off the over and get off the mark.
THE SECOND NEW BALL HAS NOW BEEN TAKEN.
Good Running. Full length delivery outside off, Kane defends it with soft hands and takes a quick single as the ball goes towards point. The lead is now 100 for the Kiwis.
Good length delivery around off, the Kiwi skipper blocks it.
On a length, Kane gets on his back foot and punches it to the fielder at cover.
Fuller this time on off, Williamson defends it strongly off his front foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson looks to cut it but gets an inside edge which bounces on the crease.
Outside off, left alone. End of a successful over, just a run and a wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gets this one to come back in just a little from outside off, Taylor keeps it out.
Ross Taylor walks in at number 4, replacing Latham.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! A lovely catch by Mithun. It needed something special to dismiss Latham and Mithun has provided it. The ploy to stick with the old ball has worked for the visitors. A length ball, just ahead of a length actually outside off. It is going away with the angle. Latham goes for the drive but the length was not quite there. The ball flies off the outside edge to the left of Mohammad at widish second slip. He dives and takes it nicely. Sarkar is delighted and end of a magnificent innings by Latham. Also, the free-flowing stand comes to an end. Can Bangladesh now make a few more inroads?
Outside off, Latham lets it be.
Back of a length around off, the batter pushes it to covers. The fielder fumbles and a run is conceded.
Soumya Sarkar to bowl from the other end. The second new ball, still now taken.

FOUR! Lovely pull shot! It is short and outside off, Latham quickly goes onto the back foot, swivels and pulls it all along the ground, in the gap in the backward square leg region for a boundary. First in this session.
On the shorter side and outside off, Kane cuts it through point and takes one.
Outside off, the batsman need not play at that.
On the off pole, Williamson stands tall and keeps it out.
A little too straight, it is clipped around the corner for a run.
Back of a length around off, Latham pushes it to mid on.

We are back for the last session! Around 35 overs left in the day. Kane Williamson and Tom Latham will resume their innings. The latter will be on strike. He will face Abu Jayed who still has the old ball in hand. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

New Zealand are cruising in this game. They have added 129 runs at around 4.50 runs per over in this session. For Bangladesh, the only thing they can be happy about is Jeet Raval's wicket. One thought, the opener's wicket would probably inject some energy into them and they would look to pull things back a little. That was not to be though, Williamson and Latham did not let the momentum slip and are amidst a 79-ball 72-run stand. The latter has crossed the 150-run mark and the former is looking well-set for a good score. The lead for now is 92 and one can say, if they continue in the same way, the lead might just near the 200-run mark at the end of today. Join us for the last session in a while.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it on middle, KW gets right behind the line and defends it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A muted appeal! Short and outside off, Williamson looks to cut but misses.
A little shape away from the batsman. The line is outside off, it is left alone.
On the off pole, Williamson guides it towards point.
Back of a length around off, Latham pushes it through covers for an easy run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Full toss but it still has to be put away! Williamson sweeps it through backward square leg and it races to the fence.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the shorter side, turns in a little. KW pushes it to covers.
Slower through the air on off, Williamson works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball and on middle, Williamson flicks it through mid-wicket and the batsmen take two.
Third leave in a row as another ball is bowled way outside off.
Another one wide outside off, easily left alone.
Outside off, the batter need not play at those.
Good length and on middle, Latham blocks it out.
Outside off, Williamson plays his favorite dab shot. The man at gully though dives and makes a half stop. Only a run.
A little too straight, Latham works it through square leg and takes a run.
The second new ball is available but it is not taken yet.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Down the leg side, Latham pads it away.
Full and around off, wristed through mid-wicket for one.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Around middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single. The lead is now worth 80.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

FOUR! Consecutive 150s in Tests for Tom Latham. His previous innings read 176 against Sri Lanka in Christchurch in December 2018. 4th score of 150-plus. Short and outside off, Latham punches it behind point and the ball races away to the fence!
Tempting line, full and just outside off, left alone.
Really nice shot. Pitched right up, outside off, Latham drives but the man at short extra cover dives and parries it to the man a bit deeper in that region.
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Another change. Soumya Sarkar returns. 2-0-12-0 so far.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and around middle, pushed through to long on for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
SIX! Wow. Nicely hit. Floated outside off, Latham jumps out of his crease and swings it over mid-wicket!
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Short and around off, turning in, worked through mid-wicket for a single. 300 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND. They lead by 66.
Mehidy Hasan into the attack again. 17-1-89-0 so far.
Around off, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

FOUR! BOSH! Short and outside off, Latham rocks back and pulls it with disdain over mid-wicket! The lead now moves to 63 while Latham moves to 140. 15 fours and 2 sixes. The stand is worth 43 from 40 deliveries.
Full and outside off, eased down to long off for a single.

FOUR! Nicely done by the batsman but not so by the fielder. Short and outside off, Williamson punches it behind point. Meidy Hasan gives it a good chase, gets to the ball with a slide, tries to push it back but while doing so, his foot touches the ropes.
We have a change. Mominul Haque to roll his arm over, with around 25 minutes to go to Tea and 4 overs to the second new ball.
Full and around off, worked through mid-wicket for three.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
On a good length around off, defended from the crease.
Around off, tucked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Around off, solidly defended.
Short and outside off, punched through point for a single.
Down the leg side, helped towards square leg for a run. Three quarters of a 100 - overs bowled now.
Fired in outside off, well blocked out.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, wristed away towards long on for a single.
Similar shot, this time Latham gets it past cover and crosses over.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! BOOM! Short, wide and outside off, asking for trouble. Gets it, does Khaled. Williamson rocks back in a flash and cuts it square of the wicket on the off side.
Down the leg side, tickled towards fine leg for a single.

FOUR! What a quality shot. A touch shorter in length, outside off, Latham just rises on his toes, gets on top of the bounce and punches it behind point. The man at deep point starts to run to his right but cannot get there! The lead now moves to 40. Latham moves to 132. The stand is worth 20 in just 21 balls.
Landed outside off, on a length, shouldered arms to.
Low full toss outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked from the crease.
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Short and around off, helped through square leg for a single.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a triple.
Around middle and leg, turned towards long leg for one. 5 singles from that over.
Around off, angling away, shouldered arms to.
Fractionally short of good length, tucked through mid-wicket for another single. The stand moves to 10 from 11 balls. The lead is worth 30 now.
Full and around middle, turned through square leg for one more.
On a length, outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Landed around off, pushed through the off side for a single.
Khaled Ahmed is back on. 16-6-46-0 so far.
Shortish in length, helped through mid-wicket for one more.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Down the leg side, helped to the leg side. The ball is stopped near the boundary and three runs are taken.
Another watchful defense.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Kane Williamson walks in at number 3, replacing Raval.

OUT! Caught! Stop the press. For a wicket has fallen. Out of nowhere. And it is the captain who has given the breakthrough. Tossed up generously outside off, Raval gets down on a knee to play the slog sweep but the line is a bit wider and he has to drag it. Gets a top edge which only goes straight up in the air. Khaled Ahmed keeps his eyes on the ball at short mid-wicket, back-tracks a touch and takes it nicely. It was not a high percentage shot any which ways because there was a long on and a deep mid-wicket in place. This is what part-timers can do. Make batsmen lose concentration and play a loose stroke. Nevertheless, a fine innings from Jeet Raval. The 254-run stand has been broken at long last, with the lead reading 20.
Outside off again, Raval mistimes his punch towards cover once more.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on for a run.
Around off, punched through the covers for a single.
Mahmudullah is into the attack now. Bangladesh trying everything.

DRINKS! New Zealand continue from where they left off before the break. They have now gone into the lead and neither batsman looks like getting out. Bangladesh on the other hand, lack intent, energy and positiveness out there. For now, it seems like they have given up and are just not interested. They need someone to provide the spark they need. Will someone put their hand up and deliver or will the pattern continue?
On the stumps, the batsman gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Outside off, Raval uses the pace of the bowler and then guides it towards third man for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Punched through covers and the batsmen cross ends.
On the stumps, defended.

Overthrows! This is poor, very poor from Bangladesh. Just gifting runs. Latham defends this to point. Now both the batsman are standing at their ends but the fielder at point for no reason makes a wild throw away from the keeper. There is no one backing up and two overthrows are taken. 250 up for the hosts.
A single to end the over! Shortish and on off, Latham stands tall and punches it through covers. He calls for two but has to settle for one.
Good length and on off, Latham blocks it out.
Drags his length back but continues bowling it outside off. Left alone.
Excellently driven but can't get it past the man at covers. That shot deserved runs.
Length and it is angled outside off, left alone.
On the fuller side on off, Latham strokes it to mid off.
Shorter in length outside off, Latham goes back and pushes it through the off side for a single.
This time defends it off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This is eased down to long on for a single.
The sweep shot is on now as the ball will be sliding past off with the angle. Latham knows that, he goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg for a run.
Flatter and outside off, Latham goes back and keeps it out. Changes his angle does Hasan now, he is bowling from over the wicket.

OHHHHH! Slightly on the shorter side outside off, Raval looks to slash at it but the ball was a little too close to the play that shot. Luckily for him though, he misses. He could have easily under edged it or chopped it back on.
A little too straight on middle, Raval works it in front of square for no runs.
Good half stop! Fuller in length, Raval strokes it nicely towards the right of the bowler. He sticks his hand out and deflects it towards mid off.
FOUR! Deft! Just a little bit of width on offer, he waits for it and then at the very end opens the face. Gets it through the gap between the slip cordon and into the third man fence.
On the fuller side around off, Raval looks to drive but mistimes it to mid off.
Raval played that late. On a length and around off, Jeet at the very end, gets his bat down and guides it to gully.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, pushed through the covers for one.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! The runs keep flowing. Short and outside off, Raval goes back and just guides it behind point for a boundary!
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run. NEW ZEALAND INTO THE LEAD NOW.
Around middle, flicked through the leg side for a single. SCORES ARE LEVEL.
Change of ends for Mehidy.
Back of a length on off, Latham pushes it to mid off.
Well bowled! Around off and angling away. Latham looks to play with a closed face but gets a soft leading edge to mid off.
Once again on the leg stump, Raval flicks it to fine leg and takes a single.
On the pads again, Raval does not get bat to it. He is hit on the pads.
Works it against the angle to the man at mid-wicket.
On the pads, Latham looks to flick but misses, it hits his pads and rolls towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
Ebadot Hossain is into the attack now.
Good change of pace there! Bowls the off pace ball on off, Raval though picks it and manages to keep it out comfortably.
Gets this one to bounce higher, it is around the shoulder height. Latham gets on top of the bounce and pulls it all along the ground towards fine leg for a run.
FOUR! Too easy! A short ball at Jayed's pace, don't think will trouble many batsman. Latham is surely not troubled as he rocks back and pulls it through square leg. Boundary.
Fullish and on off, Latham works it to mid on.
On the off stump again. Latham pushes it to covers.
On the off pole, Latham blocks it out.
Another excellent shot through covers but only for a run. New Zealand trail by only 8 now.
On the stumps, blocked.
Raval now strokes it through cover for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Latham strokes this through covers for a run.

Hesitation but safe in the end! Firstly a lovely shot to this shorter delivery as Raval plays it very late through point. The batsmen take two and then think about the third. There is a slight hesitation but then they go for it. The fielder now fires it towards the keeper. The keeper though comes rushing ahead and the throw goes over him making the third run easy for the batsmen. Had he stayed at the stumps, a run out was on the cards.
The batsman has played it to the point region.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! 9th TEST TON for Tom Latham and brought about in a nervous fashion! Consecutive Test hundreds for Latham too, following his 176 against Sri Lanka in Christchurch, in the month of December. A short ball, around middle, Latham looks to pull but is done in by the extra bounce. The ball takes the top edge and fine leg starts to race to his left, thinking he has a chance - but he never makes it. Latham takes his helmet off and shows a sheepish smile. Not the best of ways to get to a hundred but he will take it. The opening partnership goes on and on...
Around off now, driven towards mid on.
Full and tempting outside off, Latham is not lured and shoulders arms.
Landed outside off, angling away, left alone.
Around middle and leg, solidly defended.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tight, full and in line of the stumps, well defended.
Full and around middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Continues bowling it way too wide outside off, Raval continues leaving it. Jayed was guilty of bowling too straight in the first session, now he is bowling it too wide.
Goes wide outside off this time, another leave.
Closer to the off pole this time but not close enough to make the batsman play.
Outside off, the batsman does not fiddle with it.
On the fuller side on off, Raval looks to drive but it goes off the inner half to mid off.
Driven nicely but to the man at covers.

FOUR! Starts the over with a maximum and now ends it with a delightful boundary. Flighted delivery but this one is a little too full. Too easy for Latham as he strokes it through covers and into the fence. A huge over this for the Kiwis. 12 from it.
Flatter and on middle, Raval goes back and works it through square leg for a run.
Slower this time outside off, Raval waits for it and then plays it with the turn to point.
On the stumps, blocked.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.

SIX! Lovely shot! Pure timing! Latham uses his feet but does get to the pitch of the ball. He still goes ahead with the shot and lofts it over the long on fence. Moves into the 90s with that shot of high confidence.
Slants this across the batsman who makes a good leave. Another tight over by Abu comes to an end.
On the pads, clipped around the corner and takes a run.
This time the bat does not turn in his hand, it goes right off the middle but not past the fielder at mid off.
Fuller and on middle, Latham looks to drive but then the bat turns in his hand and the ball skews to mid-wicket.
Continues bowling it on off, Latham is solid in defense.
On the off stump, the batsman plays it late and defends it onto the ground.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Faster on middle and off, watchfully blocked out.
Around middle, pushed to the leg side.
FOUR! 200-RUN STAND IS UP! Just too easy, isn't it? Keep racking up the runs. Short and outside off, Raval rocks back and steers it behind point for a boundary!
Fuller in length, driven towards cover.
Short and outside off, cut through the covers for a single.
Aggression from the bowler there! He bowls it on off, Raval pushes it back to him, he collects it and then has a shy at the striker's end but misses. A maiden to begin with but not a threatening one.
4th leave in the over! Jayed goes back to bowling outside off, the batsman is in no mood to play at those.
Finally bowls one on the stumps, Raval strokes it to mid on.
Third leave in a row as Jayed once again bowls it way outside off.
A little more wider this time outside off, the batsman once again lets it be.
Starts off with a delivery in the 5th stump channel. Raval watchfully makes a leave.
Tom Latham and Jeet Raval will continue from where they left off before the break. The latter will be on strike and he will be facing Abu Jayed. Here we go...
For starters, the visitors need to ingest some self-confidence. They may be well behind the eight-ball but they need to fight. At least try to pick up wickets.
The pitch barely has shown any signs of life right from the time the Kiwis started to bat last evening and this morning it has been no different. Can Bangladesh have a different say in the afternoon?
We are back for the afternoon session! The sun is shining brightly and there is no threat of rain.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Bangladesh on the other hand, have either been too straight or too predictable. The bowlers who started off today were guilty of bowling a little too straight and hence, leaked runs. Ebadot Hossain was decent but then became too predictable with his short balls. Mehidy Hasan bowled two before the break but the batsmen seemed comfortable against him too. The deficit is only 37 and Bangladesh need quick wickets to get back into this one or New Zealand will probably take a huge lead here. Join us for the second session in a while.

Another session which has belonged to the hosts. They now are in a very commanding position in this game. They have managed to add 111 runs in this session without losing a wicket. The two batsmen have looked at ease with Raval getting to his maiden Test ton and Latham nearing one. New Zealand will hope the two can continue for as long as possible.
Another tossed up delivery on off, Latham gets right behind the line and defends it. LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Flighted delivery on the stumps, blocked.
On the pads, Raval works it around the corner for an easy single.
Gives it nice amount of air on middle, Raval pushes it to short covers.
Bowls it fuller this time, Raval keeps it out.
SIX! All the way! Picked the length early there. Short and on off, Raval is quick to go onto the back foot and he pulls it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Nicely timed but finds the man at covers.
Drags his length back outside off, Latham shoulders arms to this one.
FOUR! Straight as an arrow! Full and on middle, Latham leans into it and strokes it straight down the ground. Holds his pose for the cameras after that. Delightful stroke.
On the middle stump, kept out.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
On the middle pole, Latham works it against the angle to mid on.
Double change. Soumya Sarkar into the attack.

A huge shout but not given! Good bowling this! Got the last one to turn a little and then follows it up with a straighter one. Gets good drift into the batsman. Raval lunges and ends up playing outside the line with his bat and pad close to each other. The bowler puts in a loud appeal as he feels it is pad first. The umpire though shakes his head. The Bangladesh players have a long chat but then decide not to review. Replays later on show that it was pad first but the impact was outside off. So a good decision not to review in the end.
A little bit of turn there! Tosses it above the eyeline. It pitches and then straightens a touch. Raval does well to keep it out.
Gives it a little more air this time, lands it around off. Jeet blocks it out.
Shortish again and for the third time in a row, Jeet goes back and pushes it to mid on.
Another delivery which is fired in on the stumps, Jeet once again goes back and pushes it to mid on.
Flatter and on the stumps, Raval goes back and defends it.
Mehidy Hasan is on now. Spin for the first time today.
Back of a length and outside off, Latham looks to play away from his body but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Now follows the consecutive boundaries with a single as he works it around the corner.

FOUR! 100 for Jeet Raval, his wait is finally over. First in this format. A thoroughly deserved one, he has played excellently and he gets there with a brilliant pull shot. Once again he might have been expecting a short ball, gets it and he pulls it right off the middle through mid-wicket. Takes his helmet off and soaks in the applause by the crowd here. He would now want to score a daddy hundred.
FOUR! Crunched! Moves onto 97! Another short ball, Raval might have been expecting it. He rocks back quickly and hammers the pull through mid-wicket and into the fence.
Quick single! Back of a length around off, the batter pushes it towards mid off and gets to the other end.
On the shorter side, Raval pulls it right off the middle but straight to the man at deep square leg. Only a run.
Outside off, played a touch uppishly but it lands short of point.
FOUR! Too easy. No mid off in place and you get a half volley. Latham cashes in and drives it through the vacant space. Extra cover gives it a chase but in vain. The deficit is now 59.
Full and around middle, pushed down the ground where mid on makes a half stop.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed towards the off side.
Dropped short, around middle and leg, fended in front of short leg.
A bouncer again, around leg, ducked under.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.

FOUR! That is nicely played. Short and around middle, Latham swivels and pulls it behind square leg. There is a man in front of square leg, in the deep, but he does not even get time to move. The stand moves to 170 while Latham moves to 73. 8 fours, 1 six.
Close shave! Outside off, on a length, TL looks to punch it to the off side but gets a bottom edge which just goes on top of the sticks!
Walks across his stumps, Ebadot bowls it outside leg, Tom misses his flick and the ball just grazes the leg stump!
Full and around middle, pushed towards mid-wicket.
A bouncer around middle and leg, Latham ducks.
Outside off, angling away, too wide, left alone.
Full and around middle, pushed back defensively.
Another bouncer, ducked under again.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Outside off, allowed to go through.
Full and straight, pushed towards the off side.
Another bouncer to end the over, Tom ducks.
Around middle and leg, helped straight to square leg.
Outside off, punched straight to cover. Latham will feel he has missed out. There is only one man in front of square on the off side and he picked him to perfection.
Third bouncer on the trot, same reaction from the batsman.
A bouncer on middle, ducked under.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full on middle and leg, worked straight to short leg.
The batsman goes for the hook but misses the line of the delivery.

FOUR! BLUDGEONED! Into the 90s goes Raval, for the first time in his Test career. He has been in the zone of 70-90 5 times now and surely, this time, he should try and ensure that he gets his maiden Test ton. Short ball, around middle, Jeet pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
A bouncer, around middle, Raval ducks.
A short ball, around middle, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.

OVERTHROWS! Needless from Liton Das. A short ball, down the leg side, Raval looks to pull but is cramped for room. The ball hits his glove and goes on the bounce behind. Now, it is slightly away from Das and Jeet thinks he can run, hence, he takes a start. He is sent back but Das is not too happy, hence has a shy at the striker's end, in spite of Raval making it back. Misses the stumps and by the time mid-wicket can mop it up, two runs are taken.
Around middle and off, blocked from the crease.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Around middle and off, pushed towards the bowler.
Bouncer! The batsman does well to evade it.
A short ball down the leg side, ducked comfortably.
On a good length around middle and leg, Tom rises with the bounce and then fends it down.
Around middle and leg, pushed towards mid-wicket.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Another bouncer, calmly ducked under.
A touch short, down the leg side, Tom looks to tuck it fine, but then decides to withdraw his bat. Is late and almost nicks it behind.
A bouncer but down the leg side, Latham ducks.
FOUR! That will go through as well! Back of a length outside off, Raval gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers!
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Full and around middle, watchfully pushed back.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A bouncer now, Raval ducks.
On a back of a length outside off, blocked from the crease.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Landed outside off, left alone.
On a good length outside off, watchfully defended.
Goes right back in his crease and blocks.
Outside off, steered behind point for a couple.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! BLAST! NO BALL AS WELL! Interesting from Latham. Or was it planned? Seems to be the latter. The moment Tom hit that shot, he pointed to the field. Three fielders were placed behind square leg which is not allowed. Paul Reiffel checks with Nigel Llong at square leg and then signals a no ball. Great awareness from Tom Latham. Full and outside off, Tom hammers it straight back over the non-striker who has to duck in time. 150-RUN STAND IS UP! The deficit is now just 81.
DRINKS BREAK. Nothing happening. No swing. No seam movement. No indifferent bounce. Runs coming at will.
Play and a miss! Extra bounce does the batter in there. Short and outside off, Raval tries to cut but due to the extra bounce, he fails to connect.
Bowls this full now and on the stumps, Raval defends it out.
FOUR! Too predictable! 4th short ball in a row, this time offers width. Raval cuts it through point for a boundary.
Bowls this from wide of the crease but it is short again! Raval once again ducks under it.
Short and on middle, Raval mistimes his pull to the man at square leg. He was hurried into the pull shot.
Good short ball! The batsman evades it.

Direct hit would have been close! Short and on middle, Raval pulls it towards mid-wicket. He sets off late for the run. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. That could have been close had he hit.
Back of a length on off, Raval defends it onto the ground.
Short and outside off, Raval jumps and looks to cut but ends up chopping it onto the ground.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Another one on the pads, worked around the corner for a run.

Catch it is the call but it is well away from the fielder! Full and on the pads, Latham flicks it through mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep makes good ground to his right, slides and pushes the ball back in. The batsmen run two. The umpires go upstairs to check and replays show that he has done well.
A couple to end another productive over for New Zealand. Shortish and outside off, Raval goes back and punches it through covers for a couple.

Well bowled and very well kept! This is on a length and around off, pitches and then comes back in. Not enough though to make the batsman play. The ball however, keeps tailing in after passing the batsman. The keeper does really well to dive to his right and collect it.
Way too wide outside off, left alone.
This is where they should be bowling on consistent basis! A little more fuller though. Back of a length on off, Raval guides it to point.
Easy pickings! Down the leg side, Latham flicks it to fine leg for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Ebadot Hossain is on now.
A good nut to end the over! Short and gets this one to bounce a touch extra. Raval is a touch early as he tries to flick. It hits his glove and then deflects onto his helmet.
On the pads, Raval looks to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad.
Short and width on offer outside off, Latham stands tall and slaps it through covers. Haque gives it a chase from point and does well to save a run for his side. The trail is now below 100.
A brace! Hits it through mid on this time, gets it wide of the fielder there and collects two.
Crisply driven but can't beat the man at mid off.
Works it with the angle to the man at backward square leg.
Goes short again but the line is way down the leg side, left alone.
FOUR! Very nicely played! Another shortish delivery outside off, Raval gets on top of the bounce, uses the pace and then guides it through point.
Short, Raval hops and keeps it out.
Well played! Short and on middle, Raval waits for it and then guides it towards gully.
On the off and it is on a back of a length, Raval pushes it to point.
Good bumper, Raval is happy to evade the short balls bowled at him.
A wasteful delivery to end! Outside off, left alone.

Well bowled! However, more than the delivery, it was Latham who lost his balance. Jayed bowls it on a length and around off. Tom plants his front foot way too across, he almost seems to lose his balance but then keeps it and somehow blocks it out.
On the fuller side on middle, Latham looks to defend but it goes off the inner half through square leg for a couple.
Nicely punched! Short and outside off, Raval stands tall and punches it past the diving cover fielder. The timing is not good enough to take it to the fence but good enough to get three.
This one bounces nicely but Raval is quick to duck under it.
Shortish, this one though does not bounce as much as Raval expects it to. The line however, is outside off and Raval evades it.

FOUR! Just over! 50 for Latham. Consecutive ones for him. Also, it is his 16th Test fifty. He is making Bangladesh pay for the life they gave him. He will now want to convert this into a big score like he did on the last occasion. He gets a short ball outside off which he looks to guide through the off side. Fails to get on top of the bounce and it flies off the outer half and over the outstretched hand of point for a boundary.
Good bowling! After three short balls, he bowls it very full, almost a yorker. Raval jams it out towards mid on for a single.
Slightly ahead of a shorter length, the batter keeps it out.
Second bouncer in a row! Raval once again sits down and lets the ball go over him.
On the shorter side, Raval ducks under it easily.
Back of a length on off, Raval goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Down the leg side at 122 kph. Latham misses the flick and the keeper collects it by moving to his right. 16 from the last two overs for the Kiwis.
Short but the batsman does not have any trouble at that pace to rock back and pull it through square leg. A single as there is a fielder in the deep.
On the shorter side, Raval goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Another leg bye! On the pads, Latham fails to put bat on ball. It brushes the pads and rolls on the leg side, the batsman change ends.
Another nicely timed stroke! On a length and around off, Raval once again strokes it on the up through covers. Takes three. Runs coming thick and fast this morning for the Kiwis.
On a length and around off, Raval guides it to point.
On the shorter side, Latham gets on top of the bounce and guides it to covers. A dot to end but an expensive over, 11 from it. It has been all too easy for the Kiwis.
Back of a length on off, Latham pushes it through covers and gets two. 3000 Test runs for Tom.
On the middle stump, Raval works it around the corner and gets to the other end.

FOUR! Second boundary in the over! This is right off the middle, a shot of authority! Just behind the fuller length, Raval leans into it and strokes it on the up through covers. No need to run for those.
Outside off, Raval shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Up and over! Short of a length and width on offer outside off. Raval tries to slap it but the ball goes off the top edge and over the slip cordon for a boundary. This is now the highest opening stand for New Zealand vs Bangladesh.
Easy pickings this! On the pads, Ravail flicks it through square leg. There is a fielder in the deep so only a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
On middle, Latham blocks it out.

Another uppish flick but this time it goes past the left of the mid-wicket fielder. On the pads, Latham flicks it through that region and takes two. 100-run stand up between the openers. Ideal start provided by them. New Zealand trail by another 134.
Another one which is angled into the batter, Latham plays it with a closed face of the bat but straight to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Uppish but in the gap! First boundary of the day! This one is angled into the pads, Latham works it uppishly but away from the fielder at mid-wicket and into the fence.
Goes back to bowling length and tries to use the angle. Raval though gets right behind the line and keeps it out.

Another leg bye! The effort delivery once again by Khaled. It is slightly short and on the body of the batsman. Skids through after pitching. Latham looks to work it around the corner, he misses, it hits his body and rolls towards fine leg for a run.
Bends his back on this one and bowls it on a back of a length. Latham stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
On the fuller side again, giving the ball more time to do its bit. However, it goes straight on and TL strokes it right off the middle to mid off.
Good delivery! On a length and it angles away from the batter. Latham defends it towards point.
Fullish and outside off, the tempter. Latham is happy to let it be. Ahmed has bowled quite full but has failed to get the ball to move.
Another bouncer and once again it is ducked under with ease.
Goes short to surprise the batsman. His pace is not good enough though to hurry the batter and Raval ducks under it with ease.

Gets this one to shape in quite late but gets it to start off from middle. Latham misses the flick, it hits his pads and rolls towards fine leg and another leg bye. We did not have a single extra yesterday and we already have two today.
Better from Jayed! Length delivery and on middle, Latham blocks it out.
Goes fuller this time but the line is once again a little too straight. Raval clips it towards wide mid on and scampers across.
He starts off by angling it on the pads, Latham fails to put bat on ball. It hits his thigh pad and rolls towards fine leg. The batsmen take a leg bye.
Abu Jayed to bowl from the other end.
A dot to end! Slightly straight and the length is a touch short. Raval works it to mid-wicket. A good start for the Kiwis as 4 come from the first over.

Latham is off the mark for a today with a three! On the pads, the perfect ball for Latham to get going today. He flicks it to the right of the mid-wicket fielder who dives over the ball and concedes two extra runs.
First run for the day as Raval drops it towards mid off and gets to the other end.
Pulls his length back a little on off, Raval defends it off the front foot.

Two confident strokes to begin with but no runs! This one is also full but on the pads, Raval flicks it nicely but finds mid-wicket. He would be a little disappointed there, should have got the first runs today on that delivery.
Starts off with a full ball but no swing on offer. Raval strokes it easily towards mid on.

We are all set for the action to begin! The Bangladesh players make their way out to the middle. The Kiwi openers, Tom Latham and Jeet Raval will resume their innings. The latter will be on strike and he will face Khaled Ahmed who will start the proceedings for the visitors. Here we go...

Neil Wagner who is giving an interview says, he is very happy with his effort yesterday. Mentions it is good to work with the bowling coach, he has improved on his seam position which has allowed him to swing the ball upfront. Further adds they have the best swing bowlers going around so he wants to bring something a little different. He reckons his strength his to bowl long and fast spells and he hopes he can continue to do so.

PITCH REPORT - Craig Cummins observing the pitch says that a few cracks have already started to appear on the surface with the grass beginning to break up. In the middle of the track, he adds that the indentations are pretty big which could induce variable bounce. On the whole, Cummins feels that the surface is still good to bat on but batting will get tougher as the game progresses.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 and what probably is a very important day in this Test match. The game is now more in the favour of the hosts, however, a few quick wickets can see that change. A couple of good partnerships though will see the home side strengthen their hold on this game. Will New Zealand continue their domination or will the away side fight back? Stay tuned to find out.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

It looks like a really long day for Bangladesh on the field on Day 2 if things continue the way they are going. The pitch does not seem to have anything in it for the bowlers. The two openers look set and primed to go on for three figures each. Not to mention the batting that follows. The visitors can do nothing but just head back, get a good night's rest and try and come energized in the morning. They will hope for a few early wickets on the second day. Can they make a come back in this game or are New Zealand going to post a mammoth total? Join us on Day 2 to find out. The action begins at 1100 local (2200 GMT, 28th Feb night). Till then, take care and cheers!

The things did not exactly go the same way all day as the morning session was amazing for the away team. After being put into bat, Bangladesh scored more than hundred runs in the first session losing only two wickets. Tamim Iqbal was in his elements as he carted the bowlers around at will for boundaries. He eventually got to a century in the second session but then threw it away soon after and that saw a collapse. The barrage of short balls from Wagner and co. could not be handled by the other batsmen as they failed to defend, leave or attack those properly. The wickets fell in heaps and an innings that looked on course for 300-plus ended up at a sorry 234.

A brilliant day of cricket here if you are a Kiwi fan. What started off as a not so good day, finished in with the hosts well on top in this Test as it stands. A terrific reply from the New Zealand openers in response to the 234 posted by the visitors. They have reduced the deficit to 148 runs and all 10 wickets are still intact. Jeet Raval has been the more aggressive of the two openers and helped himself to a half-century. As for his partner, Latham has looked solid as well and ground out the Bangladeshi bowlers in the 28 overs they bowled so far.

Drinks break! This period of play has been totally dominated by the hosts. They have batted with ease and other than an early chance that was dropped at slip by Soumya Sarkar, there have been none that have been given. Jeet Raval has been creaming boundaries at will while Tom Latham has looked solid at the other end. Looks like a long, tough toil ahead for the visitors unless they can pick a few wickets soon. The last passage of play on Day 1 coming up...

DROPPED! That is a sitter. Ebadot is shell-shocked. He would have got a wicket on his very second ball in Test cricket. What a beginning it would have been for Bangladesh! Oh dear... it was bowled on a good length outside off, Latham looked to guide it towards third man but there was extra movement and bounce on this one. Hence an outside edge was induced which went straight to Soumya Sarkar at second slip. He put his hands high to try to take the catch but was not able to control it and spilled it in the second attempt. He seemed to be losing balance and maybe that was what caused the drop on the second attempt as well. That said, these type of catches must be taken at this level of international cricket.
